<think><details><summary>Thought Process</summary>
The reconciliation notebook is extensive.

The notebook will be designed for Charles to run. It saves progress after each county and resumes from where it left off. Existing parsers will be reused.

The handoff covers six jobs: inventory source families, reconcile people conservatively, check cross-county routes from both ends, verify program identities and totals, produce actionable summaries, and save and resume.

A single failed county must not halt the entire run. Missing school applicant pages should not fail other checks. Counties will not be declared scientifically ready. Name-free aggregates will be stored in the repository.

Private ledgers will remain on the Desktop. The notebook will export only counts and plain-language findings, never names.

Resume logic will fingerprint source files and skip counties whose verified work is unchanged.

Charles will handle the expensive processing. Progress will be printed conversationally.

Only eleven of seventy-five counties have complete school applicant pages.

The eleven counties with applicant pages are AB, CS, GL, TL, AR, SB, B, CT, PH, TM, and CJ.

For counties without applicant pages, the notebook will skip person reconciliation between School Applicant View and School Result View. It will still inventory families and compare school results internally.

Resident lists will be compared to school results where resident pages exist, flagged as incomplete when absent. Incoming candidates will be checked against incoming admitted and rejected totals. Outgoing destinations will be aggregated and matched against incoming admitted counts at those destinations. Program occupancy will be verified against placement row counts.

Cross-county individual matching will follow a two-step approach: first compare aggregate origin and destination counts, then report whether individual matches are uniquely supported. Full individual matching between outgoing and incoming records requires name and score keys and is treated as provisional.

Matching will run entirely in memory. Only aggregate counts will be exported: uniquely matched, ambiguous, and unmatched. No names will enter the repository.

The resume fingerprint will hash each county’s status.json slice, including saved pages, unresolved URLs, discovered lengths, and page file mtimes. Each county will be processed independently and flushed to disk.

The resume fingerprint will hash each county’s checkpoint files by path, size, and mtime, plus the manifest stat. This catches replaced pages that retain the same count. The notebook will be a single module with a directory scanner and a per-county SHA256 fingerprinter.

The notebook will be organized into focused functions. `inventory_county` will catalog families without requiring completeness. `load_verified_family_rows` will load pages or flag missing records without aborting the county run. Separate functions will handle school result structure, resident versus results, incoming internal checks, and program totals. The applicant versus results check will be skipped with an explanatory note when no applicant pages exist. Each function will catch its own errors so one county failure does not halt the entire batch.

Cross-county and individual matching are deferred passes. They require all counties to first save their outgoing and incoming aggregate counters.

Each county will write its results to a timestamped subdirectory under outputs/romania_2001_all_county_offline_reconciliation/. That folder will hold the county inventory, findings, summaries, fingerprints, and cross-county flows.

Cross-county flows may be built incrementally from per-county outgoing and incoming counters.

Each county will write its outgoing and incoming-admitted counters as name-free JSON. A final cell will combine all counties into cross-county flows.

Resume logic will skip a county if its fingerprint matches the saved fingerprint and the county JSON exists.

The notebook will have six cells: a markdown overview, settings for counties, checks, resume flag, and private root, module loading, the county loop, a cross-county combination cell, a summary table, and a results guide.

A quick syntax and import check will run first. A dry inventory of one small county may follow, but only if it is inexpensive; Alba would be too slow because of full page hash verification. The cost of verified_page and the original family manifest structure need review. Snapshot and live inventories will be compared to surface discrepancies.

The live inventory is current through 2026-10-14 11:08:40, which exceeds the snapshot date. A field-by-field comparison will exclude the refreshed timestamp.

Charles has waived notebook formatting rules. The new notebook will be created directly with Write rather than through EditNotebook.

The new notebook will use the sports_net kernel metadata from an existing county progress notebook. For counties with no applicant pages, all_gymnasium_rows will be skipped entirely. For the eleven counties with complete pages, that function will be called inside a try/except block so any directory or page errors are caught and recorded without halting the run.

A quick Python check will identify any counties with partial applicant pages. Program identity checks will catch source_programs disagreements and record them in plain language instead of aborting. The program check will read each county's manifest directly to avoid importing the full program identity gate.

Program checks will sum occupancy of admitted versus saved placement rows. If placement views are reconciled, the code will compare combined verified program row counts to that occupancy and record any mismatch in plain language. HERO or success labels will not be computed.

School result versus applicant matching will only run when both the school directory is complete and every applicant page exists for a county. It will use all_gymnasium_rows and compare name-score multisets by school code.

School result versus applicant matching will report same-school matches, unmatched applicant rows, unmatched result rows, and repeated keys. Result-only rows will not be added to the score population.

Cross-county outgoing placed counts will be drawn from school results whose Liceu suffix names another county. Incoming counts will be drawn from incoming_admitted, incoming_rejected, and incoming_candidates by origin suffix. Each pair will be compared by outgoing count versus destination incoming admitted count. Individual matching will compare name-score multisets between outgoing rows and incoming admitted rows.

Individual matching will be memory-efficient. Roughly 200,000 admission rows across 41 counties are manageable.

Only aggregate counts will be exported. These include pairs that agree in total, pairs that disagree, and within agreeing pairs the number of unique matches versus ambiguous ones.

Rows without a readable county suffix will be counted but not guessed.

For counties with unresolved school result URLs such as BN and SV, person checks will mark the check as partial rather than fail the entire county.

Saved pages will be compared directly. Any remaining unresolved school-result URL will be flagged as one unresolved address. Missing resident records will be reported as absent from the saved subset rather than from the county itself. The exact return behavior of checked_page and verified_page still needs verification.

- **Resident applicant list.** An incomplete list is a saved subset. People on missing pages are not dropped from the county and are not counted as unsuccessful.
- **Incoming row comparisons.** Printed name and admission score, with repeats kept. An incoming applicant row without an outcome row is unresolved.

```bash
cells.append(new_code_cell("""# CELL 4 — Outgoing placements versus incoming admissions. No archive requests.
if "run_folder" not in dir():
    run_folder = recon.latest_run(OUTPUT_ROOT)
flow_counts = recon.cross_county_routes(run_folder)
print("Pair rows:", len(flow_counts))
print("Saved table:", run_folder / "cross_county_flow_counts.csv")
if len(flow_counts):
    disagree = flow_counts.loc[~flow_counts["aggregate_counts_agree"]]
    print("Pairs whose aggregate counts differ:", len(disagree))
    display_columns = [
        "origin_county", "destination_county",
        "school_result_outgoing_rows", "incoming_admitted_rows",
        "aggregate_counts_agree", "unique_name_score_keys_on_both_sides",
        "keys_only_on_school_result", "keys_only_on_incoming_admitted",
        "ambiguous_keys", "comparison_scope",
    ]
    display(flow_counts[display_columns].head(30))
"""))

cells.append(new_markdown_cell("""## Cell 5 — Read the county summaries

The table is name-free. `plain_summary` is the sentence to read first. `next_source_question` is the specific gap, when one remains. A county with every known URL address saved can still be missing the School Applicant View, which is a different webpage family.
"""))

cells.append(new_code_cell("""# CELL 5 — Show the saved county summaries.
if "run_folder" not in dir():
    run_folder = recon.latest_run(OUTPUT_ROOT)
summary = recon.summary_frame(run_folder)
columns = [
    "county", "county_name",
    "school_applicant_pages_saved", "school_applicant_pages_expected",
    "school_result_pages_verified", "school_result_pages_expected",
    "school_result_unresolved_urls",
    "resident_pages_saved", "resident_pages_projected",
    "outgoing_rows_with_other_county_suffix",
    "original_placement_shortfall", "remaining_placement_shortfall",
    "next_source_question",
]
print(f"{len(summary)} counties in {run_folder.name}")
summary[columns]
"""))

cells.append(new_markdown_cell("""## What a count does and does not establish

- **School Applicant View saved / listed schools.** File coverage against the origin school directory. Person comparison with the School Result View runs only when every listed school page is present. A missing page stays unresolved.
- **School Result View verified / target.** Hash-checked pages, including the finding that a target can be a projection. Unresolved URL addresses stay open. BN and SV each had one unresolved School Result View URL address in the October 14 inventory. This notebook does not close them.
- **Resident applicant list.** An incomplete list is a saved subset. People on missing pages are not dropped from the county and are not counted as unsuccessful.
- **Incoming row comparisons.** Printed name and admission score, with repeats kept. An incoming applicant row without an outcome row is unresolved.
- **Outgoing suffix.** A School Result View destination label that ends in another county code. It is an observed admissions route.
- **Placement shortfall.** Occupancy admitted total minus the original county admitted list. Program-specific recovery can reduce the **remaining** shortfall without forcing the original gap to zero.
- **Unique name-and-score key.** One printed name and admission score occurring once on each side of a county pair. Aggregate agreement does not by itself establish that link. The masked personal identifier means even a unique key is provisional.
- **Next source question.** The concrete missing evidence. It is not a label that the county is ready for a national outcome model.

Full sentences for every finished county are in `report.md` inside the run folder. Pair counts are in `cross_county_flow_counts.csv`.
"""))

})
nbformat.write(nb, path)
print(path)
print("cells", len(nb.cells))
PY
```

```bash
    assert 12.0 <= client.interval < start

    assert 0 < cut <= 0.10

    # failure uses 1.75, not the 10% bump: reconstruct from saved interval

    before = 20.0

    print("failure factor", FAILURE_SLOWDOWN_FACTOR, "interval", client.interval)
```

_**Agent (grok-4.7)**_

You can move those packages onto conda-forge, but not by uninstalling the 133 defaults packages and installing them back afterward. Many of them are the libraries Python and Jupyter sit on. Removing them first takes the environment down before the reinstall can run, and conda will also remove conda-forge packages that depend on them.

The defaults copies you would actually notice are the Jupyter stack (`jupyterlab`, `ipykernel`, `jupyter_server`, and the notebook pieces), `matplotlib-base`, `requests`, `beautifulsoup4`, and the old OpenBLAS package that NumPy is no longer using. NumPy, pandas, SciPy, and Matplotlib itself are already conda-forge builds. `matplotlib-base` is still the defaults build, which is the split that makes an in-place swap fragile.

Do this as one solver step, in a copy of the environment, after the Călărași download is finished:

```bash
conda create -n sports_net_forge --clone sports_net
conda install -n sports_net_forge -c conda-forge --override-channels \
  python=3.11 numpy pandas scipy matplotlib scikit-learn seaborn \
  statsmodels networkx xarray joblib jupyterlab ipykernel \
  "libblas=*=*openblas*"
```

`--override-channels` tells that one command to ignore Anaconda defaults. Leave `sports_net` unchanged until a notebook has run on `sports_net_forge` and you have pointed the kernel at it.

if non:

```bash
import json, re
from pathlib import Path
from urllib.parse import unquote
p = Path.home() / "Desktop/VECTOR_temp/romania_2001_school_results_incoming_v1/status.json"
status = json.loads(p.read_text())

def shape(rel):
    text = unquote(rel)
    # drop long name values
    text = re.sub(r"(ns|nj|nume)=[^&]*", r"\1=…", text, flags=re.I)
    return text

print("SCHOOL RESULT 404s")
for code in ("BN", "SV"):
    block = status["counties"][code]["school_results"]
    print(code, "saved", block["saved_pages"], "projected", block.get("projected_pages"), "schools", block.get("projected_schools"))
    for rel, reason in block["unresolved"].items():
        print(" ", reason, shape(rel)[:180])

print("\nRESIDENT 404s")
for code, node in sorted(status["counties"].items()):
    block = node["resident_candidates"]
    unres = block.get("unresolved") or {}
    if not unres:
        continue
    print(f"{code} saved {block['saved_pages']}/{block.get('projected_pages')} rows {block.get('saved_rows')}/{block.get('projected_records')} basis {block.get('projection_basis')}")
    for rel in unres:
        print(" ", shape(rel)[:200])
    # discovered page markers
    pages = []
    for rel in block["discovered"]:
        m = re.search(r"pag=(\d+)", rel, re.I)
        pages.append(m.group(1) if m else "nopag")
    print("  discovered pag", pages)
```

```bash
        print("FEEDER", code, name)

def dump(code, lo, hi=None):
    page = saved_school(county, code, schools[code][1])
    result_keys = defaultdict(list)
    for row in results_by_school[code]:
        result_keys[name_score(row)].append(row)
    counts = Counter()
    n = 0
    for student in page["rows"]:
        exam = components(student)
        if exam is None:
            continue
        score = float(exam[0])
        if score < lo or (hi is not None and score >= hi):
            continue
        key = name_score(student)
        matches = result_keys.get(key, [])
        if key is None or len(matches) != 1:
            counts[("NO_UNIQUE_MATCH", "", 0, 0)] += 1
            continue
        result = matches[0]
        if marked_unassigned(result):
            counts[("UNASSIGNED", "", 0, 0)] += 1
            n += 1
            continue
        if (county_suffix(result.get("Liceu")) or county) != county:
            counts[("OTHER_COUNTY", "", 0, 0)] += 1
            n += 1
            continue
        options = m.base._destination_options(result, county, catalog, by_identity)
        exact = exact_codes.get(key)
        if exact is not None and exact in options:
            options = [exact]
        n += 1
        if len(options) != 1:
            counts[("AMBIGUOUS_OR_EMPTY", "", len(options), 0)] += 1
            continue
        p = catalog[options[0]]
        win = int(options[0] in winners)
        counts[(p["school"], p["category"], p["cutoff"], win)] += 1
    print(f"\n{schools[code][0]}  exam in [{lo}, {hi}): rows={n} page={page['row_count']}")
    for (school, cat, cut, win), k in counts.most_common():
        print(f"  {k:3d}  win={win}  {cut}  {cat}  {school}")

for code in focus:
    dump(code, 8.48, None)   # top 10%, boundary from the 90/80/50 run
    dump(code, 7.93, 8.48)   # 80th-90th
```

def band_of(scores, exam):
    if pd.isna(exam):

    p50, p80, p90 = scores.quantile([0.50, 0.80, 0.90])

```bash
COUNTIES = ("AB","CS","GL","TL","AR","SB","B","CT","PH","TM","CJ","AG","BR","BT","BV","DB","DJ","GJ","IL","OT","VL","VN")
```

```bash
        if key is None or len(placed)+len(unas) != 1:
            rows.append((county, exam, "unresolved", ""))
        elif unas:
            rows.append((county, exam, "unassigned", ""))
        elif placed[0] == county:
            rows.append((county, exam, "home", county))
        else:
            rows.append((county, exam, "away", placed[0]))

            result = matches[0]
            if marked_unassigned(result):
                rows.append((county, exam, "unassigned", ""))

            dest = county_suffix(result.get("Liceu")) or county
            if dest == county:

            else:
                rows.append((county, exam, "away", dest))

    if pd.isna(exam):

    if exam >= p80: return "80th–90th"
```

The congestion claim is that scarce seats, not the average classmate, are what push a similarly scoring student down. Three tests sit in the pages you already trust, and the baccalaureate files open a later, separate one.

The congestion statistic is the number of gymnasium-mates with a higher exam score than the focal student, or the number sitting above the county cutoff in the same category. Among students with nearly the same own score, in the same county, that count should predict missing the scarce seat if the paradigm is operating. The mean can stay as the picture you already have. This is the cleaner peer measure, and it uses the same applicant pages.

**2. Measure how far the placement falls, not only whether it is the top program.** The tier-1 outcome turns George Coșbuc at cutoff 8.31 and an unassigned student into the same failure. You already have the cutoff, the places, and the placement. The outcome becomes the cutoff of the program the student entered, or how many filled cutoffs sit above it. Local students stay in the denominator. A town that always feeds its own college will sit one step down, which is a description you can see, rather than a hole in the rate.

**3. Ask whether the slope is steeper where the seats are actually scarce.** This is the prediction that distinguishes congestion from a general "good peers, good outcomes" story. Gorj's top mathematics-informatics program had 100 filled places. Filologie in the same county had 25. Counties differ in top-tier places per top-tenth applicant, and you have both numbers. Hold own score fixed and compare the competitor slope where that ratio is tight with where it is loose. If classmates only matter when the seats run out, the paradigm is doing the work. If the slope is the same in a 100-seat program and a 25-seat program, the pattern is something else, including the same-town placement you just found.

Those three stay inside the 2001 Ministry pages and the rules you already locked. They do not require coordinates, and they do not drop the students who stayed in town.

```bash
/opt/anaconda3/envs/sports_net/bin/python - << 'PY'
import pandas as pd
p = "/Users/charleslevine/Library/CloudStorage/Dropbox/1-Documents/00- Dissertation/0-Next_Chapter/Code_and_Data/New SQL and PY Code/Cursor Workspace PDE/3-Master_Plan/VECTOR_work/new_VECTOR_work/education_analysis/outputs/romania_2001_competitor_count_and_cutoff_step/run_20261019T132633-0400/competitor_count_and_cutoff_step.csv"
df = pd.read_csv(p)
order = {"0":0,"1-4":1,"5-9":2,"10-19":3,"20 or more":4}
top = df.loc[(df.band=="Top 10%") & (df.county!="ALL")].copy()
top["ord"] = top.competitor_bin.map(order)
rows = []
for county, g in top.groupby("county"):
    g = g.sort_values("ord")
    # endpoints with at least 20 applicants
    ends = g.loc[g.applicants>=20]
    if len(ends) < 2:
        continue
    left, right = ends.iloc[0], ends.iloc[-1]

                 int(right.applicants), round(100*right.top_tier_rate,1),
                 round(100*(right.top_tier_rate-left.top_tier_rate),1),
                 round(right.mean_cutoffs_above-left.mean_cutoffs_above,2)))

out = out.sort_values("rate_change")
print(out.to_string(index=False))
print("counties with lower rate at the high-competitor end", int((out.rate_change<0).sum()), "of", len(out))
print("median rate change", out.rate_change.median())
```

Cluj school 101 likely omits the city because it is the default. The town extraction strategy will combine the directory name with the `ns=` parameter, normalize text, and infer locality from commas or trailing tokens after the patronymic. This approach is imperfect.

A county seat token list for the 22 counties would group schools by their seat. Satellite towns with multiple schools could be found in trailing tokens. Bucharest schools without a sector token might all map to one "BUCURESTI" market.

A last-token fallback risks misclassifying satellite towns like Voluntari or Snagov. The locality rules will prioritize the trailing token after the final comma, stripping COM./ORAS/MUN. suffixes. If no comma exists, known seat aliases at the end are checked. Otherwise the last token is taken only if it is a four-letter or longer word and not a person-name indicator. Romanian school names reliably place the town at the end.

Truncated town tokens such as TG-J should be dropped from grouping when the name is exactly 50 characters and the locality is cut off.

Schools with directory names shorter than 50 characters that end with a clear town will be kept. The next step is to write a normalizer and test grouping counts before building the heavy frame. Attaching towns via _source_frames is the slowest part.

The analysis will slice schools by exam score into a narrow p90-to-p95 band. The width of that band in score points will be reported to show how tight the threshold is.

Gymnasium crowding will be measured as the number of applicants scoring at or above the county p90, held constant per school. Only gymnasiums with at least fifteen such applicants will be included to avoid noise. Towns will be grouped only when they contain two or more differing crowding levels.

Within each town, gymnasiums will be split at the median top-tenth headcount into thin and crowded groups. If ties leave all schools in one group, or if the maximum headcount is less than 1.5 times the minimum, that town is skipped.

The outcome denominator includes only students inside the county who fall within the narrow score slice; success is tier 1.

For each town, the report will list the number of gymnasiums, the thin and crowded rates, the difference between them, the student counts on each side, and the score range. The equal-town mean of the crowded rate minus the thin rate will be calculated, with an applicant-weighted version shown separately. Towns with insufficient student counts will be omitted.

Each side of a town must have at least twenty students in the slice. At least two gyms are required per side, or two gyms total with a real size gap.

The mean exam score on each side must differ by no more than 0.15 points. This prevents comparing higher-scoring schools across groups.

The town parser will be built first, followed by the full run.

The normalizer now maps TG-JIU variants to TIRGU-JIU and CLUJ-NAPOCA to CLUJ. The locality function checks for a comma first, then strips COM./ORAS/MUN./SAT prefixes from the trailing token. If the name is truncated at 50 characters and no locality token remains, that school is excluded.

The locality function now rejects truncated names when the comma portion itself is cut off. If no comma exists, it returns None for truncated names, or otherwise takes the last token only if it is four characters or longer and not a number like NR, VIII, or XIII.

Names exactly 50 characters long will be dropped. Most TIRGU-JIU entries are shorter, so they remain.

Parenthetical suffixes such as "(PETRESTI)" will be stripped before taking the last token. This prevents a neighborhood from being misread as the town.

The last-token fallback will be restricted to tokens that appear as the ending of two or more schools in the county, or to known county seats. This prevents a single-person name such as ENESCU from becoming a false town label.

Numeric tokens such as "7" or "VII" will be rejected. Bucharest central schools that lack a place name at the end will be dropped, which is problematic because Bucharest is the best market for this test.

Bucharest schools without a place name at the end will be assigned BUCURESTI. Ilfov schools will use their own locality token if present, such as VOLUNTARI, SNAGOV, PERIS, or TINCABESTI.

A longer list of Ilfov satellite towns was compiled, including BUFTEA, OTOPENI, POPESTI-LEORDENI, and others. Bucharest schools will be assigned to Ilfov if their normalized name contains one of these satellite names; otherwise they default to BUCURESTI.

The locality rules will be validated by scanning all 22 counties for unique place suffixes and their frequencies. The comparison will run next, and the heavy county-level data fetch is expected to take a few minutes.

A single script will generate the town table. The equal-town summary will require at least fifteen students per side, two gyms per side, and a strictly greater median top-tenth headcount in the crowded group.

```bash
import re
def last_token(name):
    s = name.upper().replace("Ă","A").replace("Â","A").replace("Î","I").replace("Ș","S").replace("Ş","S").replace("Ț","T").replace("Ţ","T")

        c[last_token(name)] += 1
    print("\n", county, "truncated", n50, "of", len(schools))
    for token, n in c.most_common(25):
        print(f"  {n:3d} {token}")
```

_**Agent (grok-4.7)**_

Romania assigned eighth-graders to high school in 2001 with one rule. Inside each county, programs had a fixed number of seats, and students were ordered by an admission score. When a program filled, its cutoff was the admission score of the last student who received a seat.

The question we have been asking is whether classmates at the middle school make that harder. Call that peer congestion: a student with a given score is less likely to reach a top program when more of the other applicants from the same middle school also have high scores. We compared middle schools in the same town, inside a narrow score band, so town and own score were held fixed. The placement rates were essentially the same. The explanation below is why that result is what the assignment rule predicts.

The line that sets the cutoff is the whole county. A middle school is only a small part of that line.

Gorj is a clear case. The top math and computer science program is at Colegiul Național Tudor Vladimirescu in Târgu Jiu. It has 100 seats, all filled. The last admitted student had an admission score of 8.63. Every applicant in Gorj is in one line for those seats. The county has 3,930 applicants. If you add the top program in each of the six subject categories, Gorj has 400 such seats in total.

The most crowded middle school in Târgu Jiu is Școala Generală C. Savoiu. It has 83 students in the county's top tenth on the exam. Those 83 students are that school's entire contribution to the top of the county line. The line itself is the rest of Gorj.

Bucharest is the same fact at a larger scale. The county has 22,216 applicants and 750 seats across those six top programs. A middle school with about 20 students in the top tenth is a small share of the line.

A classmate can change another student's result in only one way: by taking one of the last seats and pushing the cutoff from just below that student's score to just above it. A student well above 8.63 still clears Tudor Vladimirescu whether Savoiu is crowded or thin. A student well below 8.63 still misses it either way. The students a middle-school crowd can touch are the ones sitting on the cutoff, and only through that school's share of the county line.

A useful table is one row per county, or one row per top program. The columns are the number of seats, the cutoff, how many applicants in the county score at or above that cutoff, and how many of those applicants come from a single middle school. That table has not been built. It will look mechanical, because it restates the assignment rule. That is its job. It shows why holding the town and the score fixed left a flat result.

One limit belongs in the same paragraph. The archived pages do not record which programs a student asked for. A student above 8.63 may have wanted a different subject. The count of students above the cutoff is therefore larger than the count who actually competed for those 100 seats.

import json

from EDUCATION_20260930_romania_2001_national_acquisition import CACHE

from EDUCATION_20261003_romania_four_county_program_identity_gate import source_programs, clean
